questions.question: What is the primary purpose of normalization in a relational database?

options.B: To reduce redundancy and avoid anomalies

questions.explanation: Normalization organizes databases to reduce redundancy and avoid update, insert, and delete anomalies.

questions.question: What is a core requirement for a relation to be in First Normal Form (1NF)?

options.C: X must be a super key for all dependencies
options.D: Non-key attributes depend on other non-key attributes

questions.explanation: In 1NF, every attribute must hold atomic (indivisible) values and there must be no repeating groups.

questions.question: When does Second Normal Form (2NF) specifically matter?

options.A: When the primary key is composite
options.C: When the table is not in 1NF

questions.explanation: 2NF requires no partial dependencies, which only matters when the primary key is composite.

questions.question: Which condition must be met for a table to satisfy Third Normal Form (3NF)?

options.B: It must be in 2NF with no transitive dependencies
options.C: Every non-key attribute depends on a partial key
options.D: X -> Y must always be a super key

questions.explanation: 3NF requires the table to be in 2NF and have no transitive dependencies between non-key attributes.

questions.question: Why might someone deliberately use denormalization?
questions.explanation: Denormalization is done on purpose to speed up read-heavy queries at the cost of extra storage and redundancy.
